actions.description: Command one or more actuated joints to target positions in joint space, optionally over a declared duration, and report whether the target was reached within tolerance.

inputs.description: Target joint values in radians, in the arm's joint order
inputs.name: joint_positions

actions.name: home

actions.description: Pause the loaded URP program with the dashboard 'pause'; completed only when the dashboard answers 'Pausing program'
actions.name: pause_program

actions.description: Stop the loaded URP program with the dashboard 'stop' (the upstream node's safety_stop); completed only when the dashboard answers 'Stopped'; not the e-stop
actions.name: stop_program

actions.description: Power the arm off with the dashboard 'power off' (the upstream node's e_stop) and confirm POWER_OFF by fresh 'robotmode' reads; it takes no input
actions.name: power_off_arm

actions.description: Re-enable after a reset (refused while latched, never run by the reset, a permit for each call): with safety status NORMAL, send the dashboard 'brake release' to an arm in POWER_OFF, BOOTING, POWER_ON or IDLE and confirm RUNNING; it never unlocks a protective stop, restarts safety or changes the operational mode
actions.name: power_on

outputs.description: Robot mode read after the re-enable (RUNNING)
outputs.name: robot_mode

facts.text: The UR dashboard server listens on TCP port 29999 and a command line ends with a newline
UR_DASHBOARD.connect opens a TCP socket with a 5 s timeout and sets connection_error on a socket error

UR_DASHBOARD.send_command sends the command and a newline, waits response_delay (0.1 s by default), reads up to 4096 bytes, prints and returns the stripped answer; it catches every exception, prints it and returns None
UR_DASHBOARD.get_robot_mode splits the 'robotmode' answer at spaces and returns the second word, cut at a newline, or the word list when there is no second word
UR_DASHBOARD.get_safety_status splits the 'safetystatus' answer at spaces and returns the second word, cut at a newline, or the word list when there is no second word

UR.get_movement_state reads getj() and returns (state, joint values): READY when there is no earlier sample or the norm of the change from it is below 1e-3, otherwise BUSY; it stores the new sample and raises URMovementError on any failure
UR.home takes a six-joint location and sends movej (movel when linear_motion is true) with the class velocity and acceleration; it returns None and turns any exception into URMovementError
The README example homes the arm with robot.home([0, -1.57, 0, -1.57, 0, 0])
keyboard_control.py documents its joint step as a step size for joint rotations in radians
keyboard_control.step_joint adds the joint step to one getj() value and sends the result with movej
keyboard_control.py stops the robot on exit with ur_connection.stopl(2)
UR.run_urp_program transfers a given local file, loads /programs/<program_name> and calls ur_dashboard.run_program()
UR.run_urp_program polls every 3 s while program_status is BUSY and counts a poll only when get_movement_state() == 'READY'; six such polls in a row end the loop
UR_DASHBOARD.pause_program sends 'pause' and stop_program sends 'stop' over the dashboard socket
UR_DASHBOARD.power_off sends 'power off'; brake_release sends 'brake release' and then sleeps 20 s

UR_DASHBOARD.initialize returns at once after a connection error; otherwise it unlocks a protective stop, or closes the safety popup and restarts safety when the safety status lacks NORMAL, switches a MANUAL operational mode to automatic, returns when the mode is RUNNING with NORMAL safety, brake-releases a robot in POWER_OFF, BOOTING, POWER_ON or IDLE, and calls itself again
UR_DASHBOARD.restart_safety sends 'restart safety', sleeps 10 s, reconnects the socket and brake-releases
The upstream REST node's emergency stop calls ur_dashboard.power_off(); its safety_stop calls ur_dashboard.stop_program()
UR raises TypeError for an empty hostname, then creates UR_DASHBOARD and the URX Connection, sets the TCP to tcp_pose, applies a base reference frame when one is given and samples the movement state
UR_DASHBOARD's constructor connects, raises when it cannot, waits 3 s and calls initialize()

measures.description: READY on the first sample or when the joint change since the previous sample of any read is below a norm of 1e-3, BUSY otherwise; every read stores a new sample, so it is not a motion-complete signal
measures.name: movement_state

measures.description: Current joint values reported by the URX connection, in the arm's joint order
measures.name: joint_positions

measures.description: Second word of the dashboard 'robotmode' answer (for example RUNNING, POWER_OFF)
measures.name: robot_mode

measures.description: Second word of the dashboard 'safetystatus' answer (for example NORMAL)
measures.name: safety_status

measures.description: Dashboard answer to 'is in remote control'
measures.name: remote_control

operator_required.name: home
operator_required.reason: joint travel limits are declared per binding

safe_state.description: arm powered off: the dashboard 'power off' of the upstream node's e_stop was answered and a fresh 'robotmode' read returned POWER_OFF, the mode from which the upstream initialize() recovers by 'brake release' (ur_dashboard.py:125-132); the URP program state and any attached tool are not checked, and after a reset the arm stays off until the permit-gated re-enable or an operator powers it on
